center.locator: mean of the three reactor-building centroids
center.note: Map centre only: mean of the drawn features' centroids; not a claim about any structure.

name: Chooz — reactor cores (Double Chooz / NUCLEUS site)
notes: Chooz A (shut down 1991) is drawn for campus context only; the Double Chooz and NUCLEUS baselines refer to B1/B2.

summary.plain: The Chooz nuclear power plant's reactor buildings — the old Chooz A unit and the two Chooz B units whose antineutrinos Double Chooz and NUCLEUS measure. The detector laboratories are not yet located.
summary.technical: Reactor-building footprints from OpenStreetMap; no laboratory position drawn because two cores alone leave a mirror ambiguity.

unlocated.backlog: Find the Double Chooz far-lab position (Double Chooz detector paper or the original CHOOZ NIM paper give the hill laboratory's relation to the plant) or an OSM/IGN feature for the laboratory entrance; then derive with both cores.
unlocated.reason: Only two operating cores (B1, B2) are mapped, so trilateration from the published far-detector baselines has a two-fold mirror ambiguity that no fetched source resolves; the far laboratory (the former CHOOZ hill laboratory) is not identified in OpenStreetMap.

unlocated.backlog: Double Chooz near-detector paper (2015) or the site plan in the near-lab civil-engineering documents; derive with both cores once the side is sourced.
unlocated.reason: Two mapped cores give a two-fold ambiguity for the ~400 m near-lab position and no fetched source gives the side of the plant it lies on.

unlocated.backlog: NUCLEUS site papers give the two core distances; with the B1/B2 footprints that is a well-conditioned two-circle intersection with a known side (between the cores) — derive once the distances are re-fetched and quoted.
unlocated.reason: NUCLEUS sits in the Very-Near-Site building between the two cores (72 m and 102 m); the building is not identified in OpenStreetMap and no fetched source gives its coordinates.
